markdown_fenced_route_rust_only.input: fenced.md, a ### component section containing a fenced ```json block with the same leading-backslash Source as source-normalization-probe/input.json
markdown_fenced_route_rust_only.result: Source unchanged: ["\\x\\foo.tga"]. NOT a C# comparison: grep of MarkdownParser.cs for a fenced ``` code-block route found nothing, so C# has no input shape to compare against here. This only shows Rust's fenced route reuses Guide::from_value/normalize_component internally; see markdown_embed_route for the real cross-engine comparison.
markdown_fenced_route_rust_only.prose_route_caveat: C#'s legacy bullet metadata parser (ParseLegacyMarkdownMetadata, MarkdownParser.cs:1001-1280, reached from ParseModSyncMetadata:900-901 when the <!--<<ModSync>>--> block content is neither YAML nor TOML) reads Source with a raw comma-split and never calls DeserializePathInDictionary/PrefixPath. Rust's markdown.rs explicitly rejects that legacy bullet form inside a metadata block ('legacy bullet metadata is not supported', src/markdown.rs:317) and has no per-instruction Source extraction for free-form prose outside any metadata block (extract.rs FIELDS has no Source/Instructions entry). Pre-existing gap, already tracked in markdown-csharp-audit.md's 'Instructions, Options and Restrictions' always-empty note; out of scope here.

markdown_embed_route.input: embed.md: a ### component section under ## Mod List containing a <!--<<ModSync>>...--> block with YAML Instructions, Source: ["\\x\\foo.tga"]
markdown_embed_route.csharp_route: ParseModSyncMetadata (MarkdownParser.cs:844-864) detects YAML (DetectYamlFormat, :904-909), calls DeserializeYamlComponent -> DeserializeComponent -> DeserializeInstructions (ModComponentSerializationService.cs:3620,3657,1425,~2136-2144), the same Source-normalization path used by plain JSON/TOML/YAML/XML.
markdown_embed_route.rust_route: markdown.rs:250-262 extracts the <!--<<ModSync>>--> body; markdown.rs:307-319 parses it as YAML/TOML and calls Guide::from_value (same normalize_component gap as plain JSON).
markdown_embed_route.result: Direct cross-engine comparison, same shape as the plain-JSON gap. Confirms the embedded-metadata Markdown route needs no format-specific handling: fixing normalize_component fixes this route too, because both engines already funnel it through their shared structured-component deserializer.

install_rejection.rust_error_guide2: Error: copy_relative / step 1 (Copy): Path must start with <<modDirectory>> or <<kotorDirectory>>: x/foo.tga (install2.log)
install_rejection.significance: Today Rust's install path hard-rejects any authored Source lacking a placeholder prefix, including the bare-relative-path authoring style the plan's own JSON probe already used. C# accepts and installs these. This is a pre-existing parity gap that blocks install for those Source shapes, not merely a dedup-comparison artifact.

mixed_case_placeholder_install.guide: guide_mixed.json (Source ["<<MODDIRECTORY>>/x/foo.tga"], preserved uppercase casing as both engines already convert it, see placeholder_case row above)
mixed_case_placeholder_install.rust_result: install exit 1: 'Path must start with <<modDirectory>> or <<kotorDirectory>>: <<MODDIRECTORY>>/x/foo.tga' (mixed.log) -- Roots::resolve's strip_prefix is case-sensitive (src/paths.rs:67), so it never recognizes the uppercase form C#'s own case-insensitive PrefixPath preserves.
mixed_case_placeholder_install.csharp_result: install (bwrap, TMPDIR redirected) exit 1: 'Source files not found... Missing mod file(s)' (csharp-mixed.log) -- C# also fails to resolve the file for this exact literal Source at install time, via a different (file-lookup) code path than PrefixPath's case-insensitive check.
mixed_case_placeholder_install.significance: Both engines fail to install this shape end to end, just at different points with different messages. No functional divergence to fix: a helper that copies source_key's existing placeholder recognition (case-insensitive match, original casing preserved) does not need to canonicalize casing to match observed C# behavior, because C# does not successfully install this shape either.

absolute_and_traversal_after_prefixing.inputs: guide_traversal.json (Source ["<<modDirectory>>/../../etc/passwd"]) and guide_absolute.json (Source ["<<modDirectory>>/etc/passwd"]), i.e. what PrefixPath's own textual concatenation already does to a traversal or a leading-/ input -- see the traversal/absolute rows under structured_source_values above
absolute_and_traversal_after_prefixing.traversal_result: exit 1, 'Unsafe path: ../../etc/passwd' (traversal.log) -- Roots::resolve/relative (src/paths.rs:14-40,61-90) still rejects the .. component after a <<modDirectory>> prefix is present.
absolute_and_traversal_after_prefixing.absolute_result: exit 1, 'Source matches no files: <<modDirectory>>/etc/passwd' (absolute.log) -- NOT a rejection of an absolute path; the tail after the placeholder ('etc/passwd') is treated as a relative path under the mods root (as C#'s own PrefixPath concatenation already does, per the 'absolute' row above), so there is no path outside mods/game to escape to. The exit is only because mods/etc/passwd does not exist in this disposable fixture, not a safety check.
absolute_and_traversal_after_prefixing.significance: The measured traversal is rejected; the absolute-looking normalized tail is looked up under the mods root and is missing. These probes do not prove all path-safety cases. Existing Roots checks must remain unchanged, and post-fix acceptance adds containment and symlink probes.

scope: Direct production-CLI JSON conversion, one Markdown fenced-block-only probe (Rust-internal, not a C# comparison), one Markdown embedded-metadata probe (real C# vs Rust comparison), two install-rejection probes, one real C# install with byte verification, one real Rust install of a C#-normalized guide with byte verification, and two post-prefix path-safety probes (traversal, absolute).
